speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing the wrist pain, and does the affected area feel warm or swollen to the touch?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. He recounts having a self-resolving left knee pain the previous week. Reports recent return from a camping trip in Minnesota. Sexually active with one female partner. No history of trauma to the wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: CBC, CRP, ESR, and Blood_Culture. REQUEST IMAGES: X-Ray of the left wrist. Are you aware of any open wounds, insect bites, or rashes on your legs or arms from your camping trip?

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC: WBC 15,000 /μL (elevated), Hemoglobin 14 g/dL, Platelets 300,000 /μL; Joint Aspiration Left Wrist: WBC >50,000 /μL (markedly elevated), Gram Stain: Gram-negative diplococci seen; Blood Cultures: Pending at the time of examination; STI Screen: Gonorrhea Positive, Chlamydia Negative, HIV Negative. Skin Examination: Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions noted on the dorsum of both wrists and hands; two lesions on the left palm. X-Ray of the left wrist: Not performed.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Disseminated Gonococcal Infection (DGI). The combination of migratory polyarthralgia, septic arthritis of the wrist, fever, and the pathognomonic "popeye" deformity or tenosynovitis (implied by lesions and pain), confirmed by Gram-negative diplococci in joint fluid and a positive gonorrhea screen, is diagnostic. Treatment should begin immediately with IV ceftriaxone.
